\section[inscribirse]{inscribirse — to sign up, to enrol}

\label{lesson:ES-C479-inscribirse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the space, then the Spanish for available.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: inscribirse}
\textbf{inscribirse} — \textquotedblleft{}to sign up, to enrol\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Me inscribo en el curso de cocina.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I am signing up for the cooking class.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La inscripción} is the registration.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inscribirse}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inscribirse}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{inscribirse}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the space, then the Spanish for available, then say \emph{inscribirse} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does inscribirse mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To sign up, to enrol\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[cancelar]{cancelar — to cancel}

\label{lesson:ES-C479-cancelar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for available, then the Spanish for to sign up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: cancelar}
\textbf{cancelar} — \textquotedblleft{}to cancel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Cancelamos la reserva.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We are cancelling the booking.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Cancelado} on a board means cancelled.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.

\section[obligatorio]{obligatorio — compulsory}

\label{lesson:ES-C479-obligatorio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to sign up, then the Spanish for to cancel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: obligatorio}
\textbf{obligatorio} — \textquotedblleft{}compulsory\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El uso de casco es obligatorio.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Wearing a helmet is compulsory.}
\end{quote}

The opposite on a notice is \emph{opcional} or \emph{voluntario}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[sustituir]{sustituir — to replace, to stand in for}

\label{lesson:ES-C479-sustituir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for compulsory, then the Spanish for in advance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: sustituir}
\textbf{sustituir} — \textquotedblleft{}to replace, to stand in for\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Un compañero sustituye al profesor.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A colleague is standing in for the teacher.}
\end{quote}

It takes a \emph{y} in some forms: \emph{sustituyo}, \emph{sustituye}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}
